clark_report.headline: I'm on the Titans at 60%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Jets offense ranks 30th, the Titans defense ranks 9th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest reason? The game is at Nissan Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, TEN have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets line gives up a sack on 10.0% of dropbacks (30th), and the Titans get home on 7.0% (9th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Titans.

other_side.title: When the Titans have the ball
body: The Titans line gives up a sack on 8.6% of dropbacks (26th), and the Jets get home on 4.2% (31st).
So the Titans have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: NYJ have allowed slightly less on a typical play than TEN this season. That makes it harder for TEN to put together scoring drives.
Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Titans defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Seahawks at 82%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Seahawks offense ranks 2nd, the Cardinals defense ranks 29th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? Over the last three games, SEA have won more often than ARI, and their scoring margin is about 34 points a game better.
On top of that, rest tilts toward SEA.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Seahawks score 29.2 points a game (2nd in the league), and the Cardinals allow 28.7 (29th).
On a typical play the Seahawks gain 5.6 yards (6th), while the Cardinals give up 5.5 (26th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Seahawks.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: The Cardinals score 20.9 points a game (22nd in the league), and the Seahawks allow 16.9 (1st).
On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.8 yards (20th), while the Seahawks give up 4.4 (4th).
So the Seahawks have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Seahawks have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest reason? The game is at Highmark Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, BUF have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Chargers score 20.6 points a game (24th in the league), and the Bills allow 22.2 (12th).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Bills have the ball
body: The Bills line gives up a sack on 6.4% of dropbacks (18th), and the Chargers get home on 8.1% (5th).
On a typical play the Bills gain 5.7 yards (4th), while the Chargers give up 4.8 (13th).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Chargers are 8th in points allowed per game (19.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Chargers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chargers score 14 or more in the first half, the Bills defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Chargers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Giants offense ranks 16th, the Cardinals defense ranks 29th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at MetLife Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, NYG have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Giants score 22.4 points a game (16th in the league), and the Cardinals allow 28.7 (29th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Giants.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: The Cardinals line gives up a sack on 8.0% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Giants get home on 6.5% (13th).
On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.8 yards (20th), while the Giants give up 5.5 (28th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Cardinals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.text: ARI have allowed slightly less on a typical play than NYG this season. That makes it harder for NYG to put together scoring drives.
Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Giants have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 72% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Giants win about 72 of them. That means the Cardinals win 28, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Giants by 7, about 73%. I'm at 72%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Seahawks at 58%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Broncos offense ranks 15th, the Seahawks defense ranks 1st. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? Over the last three games, SEA have won more often than DEN, and their scoring margin is about 13 points a game better.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Broncos score 23.2 points a game (15th in the league), and the Seahawks allow 16.9 (1st).
On a typical play the Broncos gain 5.0 yards (16th), while the Seahawks give up 4.4 (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Seahawks.

other_side.title: When the Seahawks have the ball
body: The Seahawks line gives up a sack on 5.4% of dropbacks (9th), and the Broncos get home on 10.5% (1st).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Broncos, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Broncos are 1st in yards per play allowed (4.1). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Broncos would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Broncos score 14 or more in the first half, the Seahawks defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Broncos win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 58% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Seahawks win about 58 of them. That means the Broncos win 42, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the Seahawks by 2.5, about 54%. I'm at 58%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Broncos win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Broncos at 52%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Cardinals offense ranks 23rd, the Broncos defense ranks 1st. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? Over the last three games, DEN have won more often than ARI, and their scoring margin is about 21 points a game better.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Cardinals line gives up a sack on 8.0% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Broncos get home on 10.5% (1st).
On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.8 yards (20th), while the Broncos give up 4.1 (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Broncos.

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball
body: The Broncos line gives up a sack on 3.6% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Cardinals get home on 4.9% (28th).
The Broncos score 23.2 points a game (15th in the league), and the Cardinals allow 28.7 (29th).
So the Broncos have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: DEN's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for ARI in this game.
Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Cardinals score 14 or more in the first half, the Broncos defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Broncos win about 52 of them. That means the Cardinals win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest reason? Over the last three games, SEA have won more often than KC, and their scoring margin is about 27 points a game better.
On top of that, SEA are at home.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Chiefs score 21.3 points a game (20th in the league), and the Seahawks allow 16.9 (1st).
On a typical play the Chiefs gain 4.8 yards (22nd), while the Seahawks give up 4.4 (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Seahawks.

other_side.title: When the Seahawks have the ball
body: The Seahawks line gives up a sack on 5.4% of dropbacks (9th), and the Chiefs get home on 6.2% (19th).
So the Seahawks have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Chiefs are 5th in points allowed per game (19.3). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Chiefs would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chiefs score 14 or more in the first half, the Seahawks defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Chiefs win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 61% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Seahawks win about 61 of them. That means the Chiefs win 39, which is a lot.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Falcons at 55%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Falcons offense ranks 7th, the 49ers defense ranks 32nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, ATL have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Falcons line gives up a sack on 4.7% of dropbacks (7th), and the 49ers get home on 3.7% (32nd).
The Falcons score 20.8 points a game (23rd in the league), and the 49ers allow 22.7 (15th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Falcons.

other_side.title: When the 49ers have the ball
body: The 49ers score 24.5 points a game (11th in the league), and the Falcons allow 23.6 (19th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the 49ers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The 49ers are 11th in points per game (24.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the 49ers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Falcons have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the 49ers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 55% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Falcons win about 55 of them. That means the 49ers win 45, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the 49ers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Buccaneers would erase most of the edge I just described.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Broncos at 56%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Chiefs offense ranks 22nd, the Broncos defense ranks 1st. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at Empower Field at Mile High. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, DEN have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 4.8 yards (22nd), while the Broncos give up 4.1 (1st).
The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 6.9% of dropbacks (20th), and the Broncos get home on 10.5% (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Broncos.

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball
body: The Broncos line gives up a sack on 3.6% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Chiefs get home on 6.2% (19th).
The Broncos score 23.2 points a game (15th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 19.3 (5th).
So the Broncos have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Chiefs are 5th in points allowed per game (19.3). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Chiefs would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chiefs score 14 or more in the first half, the Broncos defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Chiefs win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 56% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Broncos win about 56 of them. That means the Chiefs win 44, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Chiefs win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? The game is at Ford Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, recent form is about even.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Buccaneers would erase most of the edge I just described.

If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at EverBank Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, JAX have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

body: The Titans score 16.7 points a game (30th in the league), and the Jaguars allow 20.2 (9th).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Jaguars.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: The Jaguars score 27.7 points a game (6th in the league), and the Titans allow 28.1 (28th).
On a typical play the Jaguars gain 5.1 yards (14th), while the Titans give up 5.5 (27th).
So the Jaguars have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Jaguars defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

On top of that, ATL have been playing better lately.

body: On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.1 yards (15th), while the Lions give up 5.1 (17th).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Lions, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

If the Lions win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Jaguars at 54%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Jaguars offense ranks 6th, the Steelers defense ranks 17th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at EverBank Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, JAX have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jaguars score 27.7 points a game (6th in the league), and the Steelers allow 23.2 (17th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Jaguars.

other_side.title: When the Steelers have the ball
body: The Steelers line gives up a sack on 5.5% of dropbacks (10th), and the Jaguars get home on 4.3% (30th).
On a typical play the Steelers gain 4.9 yards (19th), while the Jaguars give up 4.7 (8th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Steelers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The offenses have been about even.
items.text: Over the last three games, PIT and JAX have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.
Two extra possessions for the Steelers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jaguars have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Steelers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 54% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Jaguars win about 54 of them. That means the Steelers win 46, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Steelers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? Over the last three games, SF have won more often than KC, and their scoring margin is about 5 points a game better.
On top of that, sF's defense has been tougher.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The 49ers line gives up a sack on 4.2% of dropbacks (5th), and the Chiefs get home on 6.2% (19th).

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Chiefs are 5th in points allowed per game (19.3). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Chiefs would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the 49ers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Chiefs win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the 49ers win about 52 of them. That means the Chiefs win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Chiefs win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The game is at U.S. Bank Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, MIN have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Commanders line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (19th), and the Vikings get home on 10.3% (2nd).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Commanders, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? Over the last three games, MIN have won more often than NYJ, and their scoring margin is about 37 points a game better.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Jets gain 4.1 yards (31st), while the Vikings give up 4.4 (3rd).
The Jets line gives up a sack on 10.0% of dropbacks (30th), and the Vikings get home on 10.3% (2nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings score 20.2 points a game (26th in the league), and the Jets allow 29.6 (31st).
So the Vikings have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: MIN's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for NYJ in this game.
Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Texans at 55%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Titans offense ranks 30th, the Texans defense ranks 2nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? The game is at Reliant Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, HOU have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Titans score 16.7 points a game (30th in the league), and the Texans allow 17.3 (2nd).
On a typical play the Titans gain 4.1 yards (29th), while the Texans give up 4.3 (2nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Texans.

other_side.title: When the Texans have the ball
body: The Texans score 23.7 points a game (13th in the league), and the Titans allow 28.1 (28th).
So the Texans have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Texans defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 55% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Texans win about 55 of them. That means the Titans win 45, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.
